# Proof of P7

We use the supplied propositions P2–P6 as black boxes. No external literature
is used. Write
\[
c=\zeta(2)^{-1},\qquad
a=4d-1,\qquad \theta=\frac{2d}{a},\qquad
\eta=\min\left\{\frac15,\frac1a\right\}.
\]
Fix \(0<\varepsilon<\eta/2\), and set
\(\delta=\varepsilon/2\). Every constant below is independent of \(x,y\);
constants denoted by \(C_f\) depend only on \(f\), and those denoted by
\(C_{f,\varepsilon}\) depend only on \(f,\varepsilon\). Constants may be
enlarged from one occurrence to the next.

## Polynomial bounds and identification of the density

The assumptions in problem.md are \(f\in\mathbb Z[t]\), \(d\ge1\),
\(f(t)\ge2\), and \(f'(t)\ge1\) for every real \(t\ge1\).
The leading coefficient of \(f\) is positive, because \(f(t)\ge2\) on
this half-line. The functions \(f(t)/t^d\) and
\(f'(t)/t^{d-1}\) tend to positive limits as \(t\to\infty\).
Continuity on each bounded closed subinterval of \([1,\infty)\), and
the positivity assumptions, therefore give constants \(b_f,B_f^*>0\)
such that
\[
b_f t^d\le f(t)\le B_f^*t^d,
\qquad 0<f'(t)\le B_f^*t^{d-1}\quad(t\ge1).
\tag{1}
\]
Here \(B_f^*\) is just a bound, distinct from the constant \(B_f\)
in the statement. In particular,
\[
\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}\le \frac{B_f^*}{b_f k}\quad(k\ge1),
\qquad y\le b_f^{-1/d}x^{1/d}\quad\text{if }f(y)\le x.
\tag{2}
\]

The coefficient of \(\log(Y/Z)\) in P4 is the \(R_f\) in the
statement. Indeed, P5 gives
\[
D_f(s)=\zeta(s)P_f(s),\qquad
P_f(1)=\sum_{r\ge1}\frac{\lambda(r)\rho(r)}r.
\]
Its asserted convergence makes \(P_f\) holomorphic near \(1\), so the
residue at \(1\) is \(P_f(1)\), which is exactly the coefficient in
P4. All the definitions of \(W_f,\Theta_f,F_f,R_f,B_f,K_f\) in P6
are those in P7. Thus P6 applies with these definitions and yields a
constant \(C_f\) such that
\[
\left|F_f(H)-K_fH^{-3/2}\right|\le C_fH^{-13/8}
\quad(H\ge1).
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(H^{-13/8}\le H^{-3/2}\) for \(H\ge1\), enlarging the
constant to include \(|K_f|\) gives
\[
|F_f(H)|\le C_fH^{-3/2}\quad(H\ge1).
\tag{4}
\]

## Reduction on an interval of moduli

For the moment let \(x\ge2\), \(1\le z\le y\),
\(2\le Z=f(z)\le Y=f(y)\le x\), and \(2\le R\le x\).
Put
\[
\begin{split}
M(x;z,y)&=\sum_{z<k\le y}f'(k)
  \sum_{1\le h\le x/f(k)}(x-hf(k))\mathfrak S(hf(k)),\\
I(x;Z,Y)&=\int_Z^Y
  \sum_{1\le h\le x/t}(x-ht)W_f(h)\,dt,\\
A(x,Z,R)&=Z^{-1/d}R^{1/2}(\log(2R))^2
       +R^{-1/2}(\log(2R))^2\log(2x).
\end{split}
\tag{5}
\]
All discrete variables in these expressions are positive integers.

We first record the correlation error with both summation lengths.
For a fixed integer \(k\) with \(z<k\le y\), there are
\(N_k=\lfloor x/f(k)\rfloor\le x/f(k)\) choices of \(h\).
For each choice, \(m=hf(k)\) is an integer satisfying
\(1\le m\le x\): integrality follows from \(f\in\mathbb Z[t]\),
and the upper bound follows from the restriction on \(h\).
Consequently P3 with exponent \(\delta\) bounds each unweighted
correlation error by \(C_\delta x^{4/5+\delta}\). After multiplication
by the positive weight \(f'(k)\) and summation over these \(N_k\)
values, the error is at most
\[
C_\delta f'(k)N_kx^{4/5+\delta}
\le C_\delta x^{9/5+\delta}\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}.
\tag{6}
\]
There are \(\lfloor y\rfloor-\lfloor z\rfloor\le\lfloor y\rfloor
\le b_f^{-1/d}x^{1/d}\) possible values of \(k\). Use (2) to sum (6):
\[
\begin{split}
|S_f(x;z,y)-M(x;z,y)|
&\le C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{9/5+\delta}
       \sum_{1\le k\le y}\frac1k\\
&\le C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{9/5+\delta}(1+\log y)\\
&\le C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{9/5+\delta}\log(2x).
\end{split}
\tag{7}
\]
The last inequality uses \(y\le b_f^{-1/d}x^{1/d}\), with its
constant depending only on \(f\).

P4, applied with precisely the ranges preceding (5), gives the two
errors
\[
|M(x;z,y)-I(x;Z,Y)|\le C_fx^2A(x,Z,R),
\qquad
|T_f(z,y)-R_f\log(Y/Z)|\le C_fA(x,Z,R).
\tag{8}
\]
The hypotheses needed here are exactly \(x\ge2\), \(1\le z\le y\),
\(Z=f(z)\le Y=f(y)\le x\), and \(2\le R\le x\), together
with the polynomial assumptions already checked. No extra arithmetic
assumption on \(f\) is being introduced.

Use P2 with exponent \(\delta\), substitute (7) and (8), and retain
the factors \(2\) and \(x^2\) multiplying the errors of \(S_f\) and
\(T_f\). This gives
\[
\begin{split}
\big|V_f(x;z,y)-[cx(Y-Z)+2I(x;Z,Y)-x^2R_f\log(Y/Z)]\big|
\le C_{f,\varepsilon}\big[&x^{3/2+\delta}
  +xY^{1-1/d}\\
 &+x^{9/5+\delta}\log(2x)+x^2A(x,Z,R)\big].
\end{split}
\tag{9}
\]
More explicitly, the two substitutions in the \(S_f\) term contribute
at most \(2C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{9/5+\delta}\log(2x)
+2C_fx^2A(x,Z,R)\), and the substitution in the \(T_f\) term
contributes at most \(C_fx^2A(x,Z,R)\). These are the last two
terms on the right of (9), after enlarging its constant.

The integral identity in P6 is applicable because \(2\le Z\le Y\le x\).
It is exact:
\[
2I(x;Z,Y)=Z^2\Theta_f(x/Z)-Y^2\Theta_f(x/Y).
\tag{10}
\]
From the definition of \(F_f\), direct subtraction gives the exact
identity
\[
\begin{split}
x^2\big(F_f(x/Y)-F_f(x/Z)\big)
={}&-x^2R_f\log(Y/Z)+cx(Y-Z)\\
 &+Z^2\Theta_f(x/Z)-Y^2\Theta_f(x/Y).
\end{split}
\tag{11}
\]
In particular the \(B_f\) terms cancel. Combining (9)–(11) proves
\[
\begin{split}
\big|V_f(x;z,y)-x^2\big(F_f(x/Y)-F_f(x/Z)\big)\big|
\le C_{f,\varepsilon}\big[&x^{3/2+\delta}+xY^{1-1/d}\\
 &+x^{9/5+\delta}\log(2x)+x^2A(x,Z,R)\big].
\end{split}
\tag{12}
\]

## The cutoff and its error budget

Take
\[
Z=x^\theta=x^{2d/a},\qquad R=Z^{1/d}=x^{2/a}.
\tag{13}
\]
We have \(0<\theta<1\) and \(0<2/a<1\) for every integer
\(d\ge1\). Choose \(x_0=x_0(f,\varepsilon)\ge2\) large enough
that \(Z\ge\max\{2,f(1)\}\) and \(R\ge2\) whenever
\(x\ge x_0\). Then \(Z\le x\) and \(R\le x\).
Since \(f'(t)\ge1\) for \(t\ge1\), the polynomial is strictly
increasing there, continuous, and unbounded. Hence there is a unique
real \(z\ge1\) with \(f(z)=Z\). If \(Y\ge Z\), strict
monotonicity gives \(z\le y\), so every hypothesis used for (12)
holds for the choices (13).

The powers in \(A\) are
\[
Z^{-1/d}R^{1/2}=x^{-2/a}x^{1/a}=x^{-1/a},
\qquad R^{-1/2}=x^{-1/a}.
\]
As \(R\le x\), the two terms of \(A\), separately, satisfy
\[
\begin{split}
Z^{-1/d}R^{1/2}(\log(2R))^2
 &\le x^{-1/a}(\log(2x))^2,\\
R^{-1/2}(\log(2R))^2\log(2x)
 &\le x^{-1/a}(\log(2x))^3.
\end{split}
\]
It follows that
\[
x^2A(x,Z,R)\le Cx^{2-1/a}(\log(2x))^3.
\tag{14}
\]

The initial-modulus estimate in P2, with exponent \(\delta\), applies
to this \(z\), since \(z\ge1\) and \(f(z)=Z\le x\). It gives
\[
0\le V_f(x,z)
\le C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{1+\delta}Z^{2-1/d}
=C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{2-1/a+\delta},
\tag{15}
\]
where the exponent calculation is
\[
1+\theta(2-1/d)=1+\frac{4d-2}{a}=2-\frac1a.
\tag{16}
\]
The other boundary contribution is controlled by (4), because \(x/Z\ge1\):
\[
x^2|F_f(x/Z)|\le C_fx^{1/2}Z^{3/2}
=C_fx^{1/2+3d/a}.
\tag{17}
\]
For all \(d\ge1\),
\[
\left(2-\frac1a\right)-\left(\frac12+\frac{3d}{a}\right)
=\frac{6d-5}{2a}>0.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus (17) is at most \(C_fx^{2-1/a}\).

Here is the complete comparison of the errors in (12), (15), and
(17) with the target exponent. For \(x\ge2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^{3/2+\delta}&\le x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon},
&&\text{since }\eta\le1/5\text{ and }\delta=\varepsilon/2,\\
xY^{1-1/d}&\le x^{2-1/d}\le x^{2-\eta},
&&\text{since }Y\le x,\ 1-1/d\ge0,\ 1/d\ge\eta,\\
x^{9/5+\delta}\log(2x)&\le
 C_\varepsilon x^{9/5+\varepsilon}
 \le C_\varepsilon x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon},
&&\text{since }\log(2x)\le C_\varepsilon x^{\varepsilon/2},\ \eta\le1/5,\\
x^{2-1/a}(\log(2x))^3&\le
 C_\varepsilon x^{2-1/a+\varepsilon/2}
 \le C_\varepsilon x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon},
&&\text{since }(\log(2x))^3\le C_\varepsilon x^{\varepsilon/2},\ \eta\le1/a,\\
x^{2-1/a+\delta}&\le x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon},
&&\text{since }\eta\le1/a,\ \delta=\varepsilon/2,\\
x^{1/2+3d/a}&\le x^{2-1/a}\le x^{2-\eta},
&&\text{by (18) and }\eta\le1/a.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
The logarithm bounds used here follow, for any fixed positive power
\(u\), from boundedness of \((\log(2x))^j/x^u\) on \([2,\infty)\)
for \(j=1,3\). Their constants depend only on \(\varepsilon\).

For \(Y\ge Z\), the defining sums split exactly as
\[
V_f(x,y)=V_f(x,z)+V_f(x;z,y).
\]
Subtracting \(x^2F_f(x/Y)\), using (12), and then applying
(14)–(19) gives
\[
\begin{split}
|V_f(x,y)-x^2F_f(x/Y)|
&\le V_f(x,z)+x^2|F_f(x/Z)|\\
&\quad+C_{f,\varepsilon}\big[x^{3/2+\delta}+xY^{1-1/d}
       +x^{9/5+\delta}\log(2x)+x^2A(x,Z,R)\big]\\
&\le C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon}.
\end{split}
\tag{20}
\]

## Moduli below the cutoff

Suppose instead that \(Y<Z=x^\theta\). Apply the initial-modulus
bound in P2 directly with its argument \(z\) equal to \(y\).
Its hypotheses hold because \(y\ge1\) and \(f(y)=Y\le x\).
The exponent \(2-1/d\) is positive, so (16) gives
\[
0\le V_f(x,y)
\le C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{1+\delta}Y^{2-1/d}
\le C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{1+\delta}Z^{2-1/d}
=C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{2-1/a+\delta}.
\tag{21}
\]
Also \(x/Y\ge1\), so (4) and (18) imply
\[
x^2|F_f(x/Y)|
\le C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}
\le C_fx^{1/2}Z^{3/2}
=C_fx^{1/2+3d/a}
\le C_fx^{2-1/a}.
\tag{22}
\]
The triangle inequality, (21), (22), and \(\eta\le1/a\) therefore
give
\[
|V_f(x,y)-x^2F_f(x/Y)|
\le C_{f,\varepsilon}x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon}.
\tag{23}
\]
Together, (20) and (23) prove the first assertion uniformly for all
the required \(x,y\).

## The power main term

For every \(Y\le x\), apply (3) with \(H=x/Y\ge1\) and multiply
by \(x^2\). Tracking the powers gives
\[
\begin{split}
\left|x^2F_f(x/Y)-K_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\right|
&\le C_fx^2(x/Y)^{-13/8}\\
&=C_fx^{3/8}Y^{13/8},
\end{split}
\tag{24}
\]
where \(x^2(x/Y)^{-3/2}=x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\) identifies the main term.
Combining (24) with the first assertion proves
\[
\left|V_f(x,y)-K_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\right|
\le C_{f,\varepsilon}
\left[x^{3/8}Y^{13/8}+x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon}\right].
\]
Enlarge one constant to cover both asserted inequalities. The choices
of \(x_0\) and all constants made above depend only on \(f\) and
\(\varepsilon\), as required. No numerical sanity checks were used
in this proof.

                                J. BRÜDERN AND T. D. WOOLEY∗

        Abstract. An analogue of the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic formula is established
        for the variance of the number of primes in arithmetic progressions, in which the moduli
        are restricted to the values of a polynomial.

\begin{remark}[Two regimes]\label{rem:regimes}
\Cref{thm:main} distinguishes two descriptions of the variance. When $Y/x$ tends to zero the variance is asymptotic to the power law $K_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}$, as in Vaughan's theorem \eqref{eq:vaughan}. When the ratio $r=Y/x$ is fixed, \eqref{eq:main1} gives $V_f(x,y)=x^2F_f(1/r)+O(x^{2-\eta_d+\eps})$, and $x^2F_f(1/r)$ differs from $K_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}$ by a factor $1+O(r^{1/8})$ that does not tend to one as $x$ grows. The normalised quantity $V_f(x,y)/(x^{1/2}Y^{3/2})$ therefore approaches the ratio-dependent profile $F_f(1/r)r^{-3/2}$ rather than the constant $K_f$. This distinction is essential for interpreting the numerical data in \cref{ch:numerics}.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Consistency with Vaughan's constant]\label{rem:vaughan}
For $f(t)=t+1$ one has $\rho(m)=1$ for all $m$, and $V_f(x,y)=V(x,Y)-E(x;1,1)^2$ with $Y=f(y)=y+1$, because the moduli $f(k)=k+1$, $k\le y$, are exactly the integers $2\le q\le Y$; by \cref{prop:density} the subtracted term is $O(x)$. A direct computation shows that for $\rho(p)=\rho(p^2)=1$ each local factor in \eqref{eq:K-intro} equals $(1-p^{-2})^2$ times the local factor of $C_1$ in \eqref{eq:c2}. Since $\prod_p(1-p^{-2})^2=\zeta(2)^{-2}$, it follows that $K_{t+1}=c_2$. Thus the constant of \cref{thm:main} agrees with Vaughan's constant in the one case where both results apply; numerically $K_{t+1}=\KVau$ (see \cref{tab:constants}). For $f(t)=t+1$, \cref{thm:main} is of course much weaker than \eqref{eq:vaughan} as far as the range and the error term are concerned. This comparison was made while preparing this document and is not part of the archived proof (see \cref{app:provenance}).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Limitations]
The asymptotic formula is established only for $f(y)\ge x^{1-2\eta_d/3+\delta}$, not throughout $f(y)\le x$. Two features of the argument fix the exponent $\eta_d$ (see \cref{sec:budget}). The cap $1/5$ comes from summing the error $O(x^{4/5})$ of the correlation estimate (\cref{prop:corr}) over about $x\log x$ pairs $(h,k)$. The exponent $1/(4d-1)$ comes from balancing the bound for small moduli, which is obtained by inserting the full variance bound of \cite{bgpvw1998}, against the error of the averaging over polynomial values in \cref{prop:averaging}.
\end{remark}

\section{Numerical illustration}

\Cref{ch:numerics} compares the theorem with an archived numerical snapshot of exact computations of $V_f(x,y)$ for $f(t)=t^2+1$, $t^3+2$ and $2t+1$, for $2.5\cdot10^5\le x\le 2.56\cdot10^8$ and $f(y)/x\in[0.005,1]$; the computations are repeated by the script \texttt{reproduce.py} accompanying this document. The constants are
\[
K_{t^2+1}=\KTwo,\qquad K_{t^3+2}=\KThree,\qquad K_{2t+1}=\KLin,
\]
computed from \eqref{eq:K-intro} with primes up to $\Pmax$. At the largest $x$ the data agree with the profile $x^2F_f(x/Y)$ to within a fraction of one per cent for $t^2+1$ and $2t+1$, and to within a few per cent for $t^3+2$, where $y$ is only a few hundred. The snapshot's empirical extrapolation to $r\to0$ is consistent with $K_f$ within its heuristic uncertainty, but it is biased by the slow approach of the profile to its limit. The numbers are evidence, not proof; \cref{ch:numerics} explains the method and its limitations.

\section{Strategy of the proof}\label{sec:strategy}

The proof follows a classical route: expand the square, count pairs of squarefree numbers in the same residue class, and evaluate the resulting averages. It has seven steps, corresponding to \cref{ch:densities,ch:variance,ch:correlations,ch:averaging,ch:dirichlet,ch:mellin,ch:assembly}.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
\item \emph{Local densities} (\cref{ch:densities}). We compute $g(q,l)$, the second moment $q\sum_lg(q,l)^2=\sum_{r\mid q}\lambda(r)$, and the Ramanujan expansion $\Sing(n)=\sum_r\gamma(r)^2c_r(n)$ of the singular series
\[
\Sing(n)=\prod_p\Bigl(1-\frac2{p^2}\Bigr)\prod_{p^2\mid n}\frac{p^2-1}{p^2-2}.
\]
\item \emph{Expanding the variance} (\cref{ch:variance}). Opening the square and counting ordered pairs of squarefree numbers in a common residue class gives
\[
V_f(x;z,y)\approx cx(Y-Z)+2\sum_{z<k\le y}f'(k)\sum_{h\le x/f(k)}C_x(hf(k))-x^2\sum_{z<k\le y}f'(k)\sum_{l}g(f(k),l)^2,
\]
where $c=\zeta(2)^{-1}$, $Z=f(z)$ and $C_x(m)=\sum_{n\le x-m}\mu^2(n)\mu^2(n+m)$. The moduli $f(k)$ with $k\le z$ are disposed of by the bound of \cite{bgpvw1998}.
\item \emph{Correlations} (\cref{ch:correlations}). An elementary argument gives $C_x(m)=(x-m)\Sing(m)+O(x^{4/5})$ uniformly in $1\le m\le x$.
\item \emph{Averaging over polynomial moduli} (\cref{ch:averaging}). Using the Ramanujan expansion, the dependence of $\Sing(hf(k))$ and of $\sum_lg(f(k),l)^2$ on $k$ is periodic modulo each $r$. Partial summation replaces the sums over $k$ by integrals over $t=f(k)$. The singular series average to $W_f(h)$, and the density term becomes $R_f\log(Y/Z)$, with the same constant $R_f$.
\item \emph{The Dirichlet series} (\cref{ch:dirichlet}). The factorisation $D_f(s)=\zeta(s)\zeta(2s+2)H_f(s)$ with $H_f$ an Euler product holomorphic for $\re s>-\frac34$ gives the residues and the value $D_f(0)=-\frac12\zeta(2)^{-1}$.
\item \emph{The smoothed sum} (\cref{ch:mellin}). A Mellin integral with kernel $2/(s(s+1)(s+2))$ and a contour shift to $\re s=-\frac58$ give
\[
\Theta_f(H)=R_fH^2\log H+B_fH^2+cH-K_fH^{1/2}+O(H^{3/8}).
\]
The term $cH$ comes from the pole of the kernel at $s=0$ and the value $D_f(0)$.
\item \emph{Assembly} (\cref{ch:assembly}). The integral produced in step (4) equals $\frac12\bigl(Z^2\Theta_f(x/Z)-Y^2\Theta_f(x/Y)\bigr)$ exactly. In the combination of steps (2)--(6), the terms $x^2R_f\log(Y/Z)$, the $B_f$-terms and the diagonal term $cx(Y-Z)$ cancel identically, which leaves $x^2F_f(x/Y)-x^2F_f(x/Z)$. Choosing $Z=x^{2d/(4d-1)}$ and estimating every error term proves \cref{thm:main}.
\end{enumerate}

The cancellation in step (7) is the reason for the shape of the profile $F_f$. All three large terms, of sizes $x^2\log x$, $x^2$ and $xY$, disappear, and what remains is $x^2F_f(x/Y)\approx K_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}$, produced by the pole of $\zeta(2s+2)$ at $s=-\frac12$.

def extrapolate(rows,xs,passing):
    if not passing:
        return {'value':None,'uncertainty':None,'method':'No suffix of ratio grid passes the 1% stability test; no empirical limit reported.','ratio_cutoff':None,'cutoff_sensitivity':'Not applicable.'}
    cutoff=passing[0]
    def one_fit(idx,x,model,upper_ratio=1.):
        threshold=.005 if idx<0 else RATIOS[idx]
        rr=[r for r in rows if r['x']==x and threshold<=r['ratio_target']<=upper_ratio]
        t=np.array([r['ratio_actual'] for r in rr]);z=np.array([r['normalised'] for r in rr])
        if model=='sqrt+linear': A=np.column_stack([np.ones(len(t)),np.sqrt(t),t])
        elif model=='sqrt': A=np.column_stack([np.ones(len(t)),np.sqrt(t)])
        else: A=np.column_stack([np.ones(len(t)),np.sqrt(t),t,t**1.5])
        if len(t)<=A.shape[1]:return None
        cf=np.linalg.lstsq(A,z,rcond=None)[0];e=z-A@cf
        cov=np.linalg.inv(A.T@A)*(e@e)/(len(t)-A.shape[1])
        return dict(value=float(cf[0]),intercept_se=float(math.sqrt(cov[0,0])),coefficients=cf.tolist(),residual_rms=float(np.sqrt(np.mean(e*e))),n=len(t),x=x,model=model,ratio_cutoff=threshold,upper_ratio=upper_ratio)
    primary=one_fit(cutoff,xs[-1],'sqrt+linear')
    if primary is None:
        return {'value':None,'uncertainty':None,'method':'Stable suffix has too few points for the three-parameter extrapolation plus residual degrees of freedom.','ratio_cutoff':RATIOS[cutoff],'cutoff_sensitivity':'No adequately determined fit.'}
    variants=[]
    lower=-1 if cutoff==0 and any(r['ratio_target']==.005 and r['x']==xs[-1] for r in rows) else max(0,cutoff-1)
    for idx in sorted(set([lower,cutoff,min(len(RATIOS)-1,cutoff+1)])):
        fit=one_fit(idx,xs[-1],'sqrt+linear')
        if fit:variants.append(fit)
    previous=one_fit(cutoff,xs[-2],'sqrt+linear')
    alternatives=[one_fit(cutoff,xs[-1],m) for m in ['sqrt','sqrt+linear+threehalves']]
    alternatives=[v for v in alternatives if v]
    windowfits=[one_fit(cutoff,xs[-1],'sqrt+linear',upper) for upper in [.1,.2,.4]]
    windowfits=[v for v in windowfits if v]
    deviations=[abs(v['value']-primary['value']) for v in variants+alternatives+windowfits+([previous] if previous else [])]
    sensitivity=max([abs(v['value']-primary['value']) for v in variants]+[0])
    spread=max(v['value'] for v in variants)-min(v['value'] for v in variants)
    uncertainty=max([2*primary['intercept_se'],spread]+deviations)
    return dict(value=primary['value'],uncertainty=uncertainty,method='Unweighted least squares N(r)=C+a*sqrt(r)+b*r using only largest-x rows at/above stable-suffix cutoff. Uncertainty=max(2 formal intercept SE, full neighboring-cutoff spread, previous-x shift, alternative-model shifts, upper-ratio-window shifts for r_max=.1,.2,.4 when determined); heuristic, not a confidence interval.',ratio_cutoff=RATIOS[cutoff],cutoff_sensitivity=f'Maximum absolute intercept shift upon moving cutoff one grid step: {sensitivity:.12g}; full range across cutoff fits: {spread:.12g}. See cutoff_fits (lower adjacent cutoff may fail stability).',cutoff_spread=spread,primary_fit=primary,cutoff_fits=variants,previous_x_fit=previous,alternative_models=alternatives,upper_ratio_window_fits=windowfits)

## Common notation and coefficient interfaces

Write
\[
c=\zeta(2)^{-1},\quad d=\deg f,\quad Y=f(y),\quad
a=4d-1,\quad \eta=\min\{1/5,1/a\}.
\]
Use \(\mathfrak S,\lambda,W_f,D_f,P_f,H_f,\Theta_f,F_f\) exactly as
defined in P1 and P4–P6. The following identifications are essential:

* P1's \(\lambda(r)=\varphi(r)c^2G(r)^2\) is precisely the
  cube-free-supported function in P4 and P5, including \(\lambda(1)=c^2\).
* The singular series and the local factors of \(W_f\) agree in P3–P6.
  In particular, \(\rho(1)=1\) handles primes with \(p^2\mid h\).
* P5 supplies
  \[
  R_f=P_f(1)=\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}D_f(s)
      =\sum_{r\ge1}\lambda(r)\rho(r)/r.
  \]
  Thus P4's density coefficient is exactly P6's residue, rather than
  another coefficient requiring an approximation.
* Writing \(L_f\) for the constant Laurent coefficient of \(D_f\) at one,
  P5 gives \(L_f=\gamma_E R_f+P_f'(1)\); hence both definitions give
  \(B_f=L_f-3R_f/2\).
* At \(s=-1/2\),
  \[
  \operatorname{Res}D_f(s)=\tfrac12\zeta(-1/2)H_f(-1/2),\qquad
  K_f=-\tfrac{16}{3}\operatorname{Res}D_f(s)
      =-\tfrac83\zeta(-1/2)H_f(-1/2)>0.
  \]
  The factor \(1/2\) comes from \(\zeta(2s+2)\). P5 also gives
  \(D_f(0)=-c/2\), consistent with the positive \(cH\) term in P6.

## Composition before choosing the cutoffs

Fix \(0<\varepsilon<\eta/2\), and apply P2 and P3 with the smaller
exponent \(e=\varepsilon/2\). All constants below depend at most on
\(f,\varepsilon\). Initially suppose
\[
1\le z\le y,\qquad 2\le Z=f(z)\le Y\le x,\qquad 2\le R\le x.
\]
Define
\[
\begin{split}
M&=\sum_{z<k\le y}f'(k)\sum_{1\le h\le x/f(k)}
             (x-hf(k))\mathfrak S(hf(k)),\\
I&=\int_Z^Y\sum_{1\le h\le x/t}(x-ht)W_f(h)\,dt,\\
A&=Z^{-1/d}R^{1/2}(\log(2R))^2
      +R^{-1/2}(\log(2R))^2\log(2x).
\end{split}
\]
The polynomial assumptions give \(f(t)\asymp_f t^d\),
\(f'(t)\ll_f t^{d-1}\), and therefore
\[
\sum_{z<k\le y}\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}\ll_f\log(2x).
\]
For every pair \((k,h)\) in these sums, \(m=hf(k)\) is an integer
in \([1,x]\), as required by P3. Its error is uniform in this entire
range, including \(m\) close to \(x\). Summing that error gives
\[
\begin{split}
|S_f-M|
&\le C_e x^{4/5+e}\sum_{z<k\le y}f'(k)\lfloor x/f(k)\rfloor\\
&\ll_{f,e}x^{9/5+e}\log(2x).
\end{split}
\]
P4 separately gives
\[
M=I+O_f(x^2A),\qquad T_f=R_f\log(Y/Z)+O_f(A).
\]
Consequently P2 implies
\[
\begin{split}
V_f(x;z,y)
={}&cx(Y-Z)+2I-x^2R_f\log(Y/Z)\\
&+O_{f,e}\left(x^{3/2+e}+xY^{1-1/d}
                     +x^{9/5+e}\log(2x)+x^2A\right).
\tag{1}
\end{split}
\]
In detail, the correlation substitution contributes twice its bound;
the off-diagonal averaging contributes \(2O_f(x^2A)\), and density
averaging contributes \(-x^2O_f(A)\). These constants are absorbed in
(1); no error has been omitted.

P6's integral identity is exact:
\[
2I=Z^2\Theta_f(x/Z)-Y^2\Theta_f(x/Y).
\]
The definition
\[
F_f(H)=R_f\log H+B_f+c/H-\Theta_f(H)/H^2
\]
then gives the exact cancellation
\[
\begin{split}
cx(Y-Z)+2I-x^2R_f\log(Y/Z)
=x^2\{F_f(x/Y)-F_f(x/Z)\}.
\end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
The \(B_f\) terms cancel, and the signs of both the logarithm and
diagonal terms agree. By P6, uniformly for \(H\ge1\),
\[
F_f(H)=K_fH^{-3/2}+O_f(H^{-13/8}),\qquad
|F_f(H)|\ll_f H^{-3/2}.
\tag{3}
\]
Splitting the original sum at the real point \(z\), and using P2 on
the initial part, (1)–(3) now yield the full unoptimized error budget
\[
\boxed{\begin{split}
V_f(x,y)=x^2F_f(x/Y)+O_{f,e}\big(&x^{3/2+e}
 +xY^{1-1/d}+x^{9/5+e}\log(2x)\\
 &+x^2Z^{-1/d}R^{1/2}(\log(2R))^2\\
 &+x^2R^{-1/2}(\log(2R))^2\log(2x)\\
 &+x^{1+e}Z^{2-1/d}+x^{1/2}Z^{3/2}\big).
\end{split}}
\tag{4}
\]
The last two errors respectively dispose of \(V_f(x,z)\) and
\(x^2F_f(x/Z)\). Alternatively, expanding that boundary profile by
(3) gives a boundary main term \(K_fx^{1/2}Z^{3/2}\) and error
\(O_f(x^{3/8}Z^{13/8})\). The latter is bounded by the last term
of (4), since \((Z/x)^{1/8}\le1\).

## Cutoff choices and every exponent

Take
\[
\theta=\frac{2d}{4d-1}=\frac{2d}{a},\qquad
Z=x^\theta,\qquad R=Z^{1/d}=x^{2/a}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(x\), depending only on \(f\),
\(Z\ge f(1)\), \(Z\ge2\), and \(R\ge2\).
Both cutoff powers are strictly less than one. Since \(f'\ge1\),
there is a unique real \(z\ge1\) with \(f(z)=Z\); if \(Y\ge Z\),
then \(z\le y\). Thus all hypotheses of P2, P4, and P6 hold.

The errors of (4) specialize as follows, retaining logarithmic losses:

| Origin | Bound after choosing the cutoffs |
|---|---|
| P2 variance reduction | \(x^{3/2+e}\) |
| P2 polynomial endpoint | \(xY^{1-1/d}\le x^{2-1/d}\) |
| P3 summed correlation error | \(x^{9/5+e}\log(2x)\) |
| P4 finite spectral sum | \(x^{2-1/a}(\log(2R))^2\) |
| P4 spectral tail | \(x^{2-1/a}(\log(2R))^2\log(2x)\) |
| P2 initial moduli | \(x^{1+e}Z^{2-1/d}=x^{2-1/a+e}\) |
| Lower profile boundary | \(x^{1/2}Z^{3/2}=x^{1/2+3d/a}\) |

For the last row,
\[
2-1/a-(1/2+3d/a)=\frac{6d-5}{2a}>0.
\]
Also \(\eta\le1/5\), \(\eta\le1/a\), and \(\eta\le1/d\).
Use \(\log(2x)\ll_\varepsilon x^{\varepsilon/2}\) in the P3 row,
and \((\log(2x))^3\ll_\varepsilon x^{\varepsilon/2}\) in the P4 rows.
Since \(e=\varepsilon/2\), every row is
\(O_{f,\varepsilon}(x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon})\). This proves
\[
V_f(x,y)=x^2F_f(x/Y)+O_{f,\varepsilon}(x^{2-\eta+\varepsilon})
\tag{5}
\]
when \(Y\ge Z\).

If \(Y<Z\), apply P2 directly at \(y\):
\[
V_f(x,y)\ll_{f,e}x^{1+e}Y^{2-1/d}
 \le x^{2-1/a+e}O_{f,e}(1).
\]
At the same time (3) gives
\[
x^2|F_f(x/Y)|\ll_f x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}
 \le x^{1/2+3d/a}O_f(1).
\]
The same exponent comparisons prove (5) in this case too. Real \(y\)
and \(z\) cause no further error: the discrete sums split exactly with
the conventions \(k\le z\) and \(z<k\le y\), and the propositions
already include real endpoints and the error \(xY^{1-1/d}\).

Finally, (3) at \(H=x/Y\), multiplied by \(x^2\), gives exactly
\[
x^2F_f(x/Y)=K_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}
                 +O_f(x^{3/8}Y^{13/8}).
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (5) and (6) is the second estimate of P7 and of the plan.

## Numerical constant and independent checks

For convenient numerical evaluation, set
\[
\alpha_p=1-2/p^2+\rho(p^2)/p^4,\quad
\beta_p=\rho(p)/p^3-\rho(p^2)/p^4,\quad
\delta_p=1/p^2-\rho(p)/p^3.
\]
The grouped local factor at the relevant point is
\[
L_p=(1-1/p)(\alpha_p+\beta_p\sqrt p+\delta_pp),\qquad
K_f=-\tfrac83\zeta(-1/2)\prod_p L_p.
\tag{7}
\]
This is algebraically the Euler product in P5, with its normalization
and residue factor retained.

For \(f(t)=t^2+1\), \(\rho(2)=1\), \(\rho(4)=0\); for odd primes,
\(\rho(p)=\rho(p^2)=2\) if \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), and both are zero
otherwise. For \(f(t)=t^3+2\), the exceptional pairs
\((\rho(p),\rho(p^2))\) at \(p=2,3\) are both \((1,0)\).
For \(p>3\), the two root counts agree; they are one if
\(p\equiv2\pmod3\), and otherwise three or zero according as
\((-2)^{(p-1)/3}\equiv1\pmod p\) or not. Simple roots have unique
lifts modulo \(p^2\), as follows directly by expanding
\(f(u+pv)\) modulo \(p^2\).

A sieve and these modular tests give the following partial products:

| Prime cutoff | \(K_{t^2+1}\) | \(K_{t^3+2}\) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| \(10^4\) | 0.138088026876 | 0.135612819679 |
| \(10^5\) | 0.138083068192 | 0.135607953971 |
| \(10^6\) | 0.138082663035 | 0.135607555131 |
| \(10^7\) | 0.138082628837 | 0.135607521554 |

For a conservative truncation bound, beyond this cutoff both root
counts are at most three. Expanding (7) shows
\(|L_p-1|\le15/p^2\). Thus the omitted product differs from one by at
most \(\exp(15/N)-1\), using
\(\sum_{p>N}p^{-2}\le\sum_{n>N}n^{-2}\le1/N\).
At \(N=10^7\), this bounds the absolute truncation error in these
constants by \(2.08\times10^{-7}\) and \(2.04\times10^{-7}\),
respectively. These bounds concern truncation; numerical evaluation
used extended precision for the product and 40-digit zeta evaluation,
without a formal interval-arithmetic rounding certificate.

Accordingly the predicted small-ratio main terms are
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
f(k)=k^2+1:& V_f(x,y)\sim0.138083\,x^{1/2}(y^2+1)^{3/2},\\
f(k)=k^3+2:& V_f(x,y)\sim0.135608\,x^{1/2}(y^3+2)^{3/2},
\end{array}
\]
in the asymptotic range specified below. Comparing with
`constant_extrapolated`, rather than a fixed-ratio row, gives:

| Polynomial | Analytic constant, cutoff \(10^7\) | Extrapolated constant | Heuristic uncertainty | Relative discrepancy \((K-C)/C\) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| \(k^2+1\) | 0.138082628837 | 0.134474705492 | 0.007284958561 | +2.68298% |
| \(k^3+2\) | 0.135607521554 | 0.136321256839 | 0.002403606058 | −0.52357% |

Both differences are inside the recorded heuristic bands (0.4953
and 0.2969 times their respective half-widths). There is no clean-factor
discrepancy. The bands are not rigorous confidence intervals or bounds
on the theorem's remainder.

I independently reconstructed the primary extrapolation by taking the
largest-\(x\) rows with target ratio at least 0.01 and fitting
\(N(r)=C+a\sqrt r+br\) by unweighted least squares, using the actual
ratios as arguments. The coefficient vectors reproduce the snapshot:
\[
\begin{split}
t^2+1:&\quad(0.13447470549221466,\ 0.05829819823814369,
                                  -0.020881393324478102),\\
t^3+2:&\quad(0.13632125683949853,\ 0.037554586806314995,
                                  -0.006861994814706394).
\end{split}
\]
No numerical implementation source was supplied in the working directory.
As an independent check of the snapshot's counting and density conventions,
I sieved squarefree integers through \(x=250000\), counted every residue
class directly for all \(k\le49\) in the quadratic case and \(k\le13\)
in the cubic case, and evaluated P1's local density factors as exact
rationals times \(c\). If \(b(q,l)=g(q,l)/c\), the checked decomposition is
\[
V=A-2xcB+x^2c^2D,\quad
A=\sum_k f'(k)\sum_l Q^2,\quad
B=\sum_k f'(k)\sum_l Qb,\quad
D=\sum_k f'(k)\sum_l b^2.
\]
Here the snapshot's `B_decimal` and `D_decimal` represent these rational
coefficients before multiplication by \(c\) and \(c^2\). Both integer
\(A\)'s agree exactly, the rational coefficients agree to the stored
precision, and 70-digit evaluation gives
\[
\begin{split}
V_{t^2+1}(250000,49)&=8396479.996849530485497723\ldots,\\
V_{t^3+2}(250000,13)&=8245012.516153072373414919\ldots,
\end{split}
\]
matching the supplied rows. This spot check and the reproduced fits do
not constitute an audit of every production count or of the full
heuristic uncertainty calculation.

For a fixed positive \(r=Y/x\), the theorem predicts \(x^2F_f(1/r)\).
In particular, its power-main-term error, divided by
\(x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\), is \(O_f(r^{1/8})\), which need not vanish as
\(x\) increases at fixed \(r\). This is why individual fixed-ratio
rows cannot be used as measurements of \(K_f\).

## Final theorem and comparison with the plan

Let \(f\in\mathbb Z[t]\) have degree \(d\ge1\), with
\(f(t)\ge2\) and \(f'(t)\ge1\) for real \(t\ge1\), and retain the
original variance and original weight \(f'(k)\). Set \(Y=f(y)\),
\(\eta_d=\min\{1/5,1/(4d-1)\}\), and define \(F_f\) as above and
\(K_f>0\) by (7). For every \(0<\varepsilon<\eta_d/2\), uniformly
for real \(x\ge x_0(f,\varepsilon)\), \(y\ge1\), and \(Y\le x\),
\[
\boxed{V_f(x,y)=x^2F_f(x/Y)
                 +O_{f,\varepsilon}(x^{2-\eta_d+\varepsilon})}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{V_f(x,y)=K_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}
 +O_{f,\varepsilon}\left(x^{3/8}Y^{13/8}
                           +x^{2-\eta_d+\varepsilon}\right).}
\]
For any fixed \(0<\delta<\eta_d/3\), choose
\(\varepsilon=\delta/2\). Dividing the second estimate by its
positive main term yields
\[
\left|\frac{V_f(x,y)}{K_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}}-1\right|
\ll_{f,\delta}(Y/x)^{1/8}
             +x^{3/2-\eta_d+\delta/2}Y^{-3/2}.
\]
On the range
\[
x^{1-2\eta_d/3+\delta}\le Y\le x^{1-\delta},
\]
the two terms are at most \(x^{-\delta/8}\) and \(x^{-\delta}\).
Thus the plan's claimed relative error \(O_{f,\delta}(x^{-\delta/8})\)
follows as well. In particular the lower exponents are
\(19/21+\delta\) for the quadratic and \(31/33+\delta\) for the cubic.
The range is nonempty because \(\delta<\eta_d/3\).

There are no interface mismatches and no loss relative to the chosen
plan. The two limitations already present in the plan are visible in
the budget: summing P3 caps the saving at \(1/5\), and balancing P2's
initial-modulus bound with P4's averaging error gives \(1/(4d-1)\).
No irreducibility, discriminant, content, or squarefreeness restriction
on the polynomial is added.

}# Sparse variance for squarefree numbers — write-up of archived run `zt-thesis-plan`

This directory contains a LaTeX account of the proof archived in `../source/`
(selected plan `thesis@gpt-6.1-sol`, archive commit
`867fc9baf25edf4995748d91dd950e98cfd9debf`), together with the script that
recomputes every number in its tables and figures.

## Files

- `main.tex`, `chapters/*.tex`: the manuscript (report class, 10 chapters + 2 appendices).
- `references.bib`: bibliography (BibTeX, style `amsplain`).
- `reproduce.py`: standalone numerical entry point.
- `generated/`: tables (`tab_*.tex`), pgfplots figures (`fig_*.tex`), plot data
  (`*.dat`) and constant macros (`constants.tex`), all written by `reproduce.py`.
- `reproduction.json`: machine-readable summary written by `reproduce.py`
  (`artifacts` lists every generated file relative to this directory; also
  parameters, fits, uncertainties, the consistency check against the archived
  snapshot, and the environment).
- `changes.md`: map from every statement to its archived proposition, proof
  and reviews; notation changes, merged arguments, corrections, added material
  and the revision history.

`reproduce.py` writes nothing else inside `manuscript/`: the snapshot code runs
in a separate build directory (see below).

## Reproduction

From the **workspace root** (the directory containing `source/` and `manuscript/`):

```sh
python3 manuscript/reproduce.py
```

Requirements: Python 3 with `numpy`, `scipy` and `mpmath`; `clang++` with C++17
support (the snapshot code calls `clang++ -O3 -std=c++17`). No network access
and no installation are needed. The full run recomputes the archived snapshot
grid (x up to 2.56·10^8) and took 11–14 minutes and roughly 5 GB of memory
on an Apple M2 Pro. What it does:

1. Copies `source/numerics/snapshot/compute.py` and `counts.cpp` unchanged into
   a fresh temporary directory created by Python's `tempfile` (normally under
   `$TMPDIR`; the script refuses to build inside `manuscript/`), checks their SHA-256 against
   `source/numerics/accepted.json`, compiles the C++ worker locally there and
   runs the snapshot pipeline (`compute.main()`), including its validations
   and fits. The snapshot code writes its worker binary, per-x caches,
   `results.json` and `report.md` into that directory, which is deleted when
   the script ends. Nothing under `source/` is written.
2. Compares the recomputed rows with the archived `results.json` (exact integer
   counts and 70-digit values); the result is stored in `reproduction.json`
   under `snapshot.consistency_with_archived_results`.
3. Evaluates R_f, B_f, H_f(-1/2), K_f, W_f(h), Θ_f(H), F_f(H) from their
   Euler products (primes ≤ 10^7) and definitions, compares the data with the
   predicted profile, and applies the snapshot's own extrapolation routine to
   the exact profile.
4. Writes `generated/*` and `reproduction.json`.

Options: `--quick` (x ≤ 4·10^6 only; a pipeline test, whose tables differ from
the manuscript and overwrite `generated/`), `--build-dir DIR` (keep the
snapshot build in `DIR`, which must lie outside `manuscript/`, instead of a
temporary directory), `--reuse` (with `--build-dir`: reuse the per-x caches
there), `--pmax N` (prime cutoff for the Euler products).

## Compilation

```sh
cd manuscript
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -no-shell-escape main.tex
```

Packages used: amsmath/amssymb/amsthm/mathtools, thmtools, booktabs, enumitem,
microtype, geometry, xcolor, pgfplots (with the `groupplots` library),
hyperref, cleveref. No shell escape is needed. `main.tex` inputs the files in
`generated/`, so `reproduce.py` must have been run first (the generated files
from the run used to prepare this document are included).

  bibliography candidate list. Data for Mirsky (1949) come from the candidate

- **Numerics.** All fitted constants and uncertainty envelopes are heuristic.
